nodes.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$ and $\delta$, including $\delta = 0$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,\delta} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ is continuous.
nodes.title: Continuity of the interval cutoff

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$ and $x$ with $\delta > 0$ and $a + \delta \le x \le b - \delta$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,\delta}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ satisfies $\chi_{a,b,\delta}(x) = 1$.
nodes.title: The interval cutoff equals one on its plateau

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$ and $\delta$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,\delta}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ satisfies $\chi_{a,b,\delta}(a) = 0$.
nodes.title: The interval cutoff vanishes at the left endpoint

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$ and $x$ with $\delta > 0$ and $b \le x$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,\delta}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ satisfies $\chi_{a,b,\delta}(x) = 0$.
nodes.title: The interval cutoff vanishes right of the interval

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$ and $x$ with $\delta > 0$ and $x \le a$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,\delta}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ satisfies $\chi_{a,b,\delta}(x) = 0$.
nodes.title: The interval cutoff vanishes left of the interval

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$ and $\delta$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,\delta}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ satisfies $\chi_{a,b,\delta}(b) = 0$.
nodes.title: The interval cutoff vanishes at the right endpoint

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$ and $x$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,\delta}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ satisfies $\chi_{a,b,\delta}(x) \le 1$.
nodes.title: The interval cutoff is at most one

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$ and $x$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,\delta}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ satisfies $0 \le \chi_{a,b,\delta}(x)$.
nodes.title: The interval cutoff is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$ and $x$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,0}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $0$ satisfies $\chi_{a,b,0}(x) = 0$.
nodes.title: The interval cutoff of zero width vanishes

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$, $b$ and $\delta$, the interval cutoff is the function $\chi_{a,b,\delta} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by
nodes.title: Interval cutoff

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
